text: ← Foundations contents THE LEARNING PATH WHAT YOU WILL LEARNDistinguish equalities from estimates and calculate how a quantity scales. 01Start with “by what factor?” A sphere has area A = 4πR². Replace R by 2R to find how the area changes. Ratios like this are one of the most useful tools in astrophysics. A' = 4π(2R)2 = 4 × 4πR2 = 4A The notation a ∝ bⁿ means a = Cbⁿ with the constant C omitted. Check that C stays fixed before using a scaling relation. 02Combine powers and clear denominators R4(MR)4 = R4M4R4 = M4 You may multiply or divide both sides by the same quantity, provided you never divide by zero. A fractional power M1/3 is a cube root; M2/3 is its square. 03Four symbols with different jobs = is an equality within a model; ≈ an approximation; ∼ an order-of-magnitude estimate with coefficients omitted; ∝ a scaling under fixed conditions. An estimate cannot determine an exact coefficient. 04Units are part of the equation We generally use SI: metres, seconds, kilograms, kelvin, joules, and watts (joules per second). Useful reference scales are M☉ ≈ 1.99 × 10³⁰ kg and L☉ ≈ 3.83 × 10²⁶ W. 1 eV = 1.602 × 10−19 J The electronvolt is a unit of energy. Temperature conversions use T[K] = t[°C] + 273.15. exp(x) means eˣ, with e ≈ 2.718. The natural logarithm reverses it: ln(eˣ) = x. If these functions are new to you, start with the numerical examples. 05Keep these constants at hand c: speed of light. G: gravitational constant. h: Planck’s constant, converting photon frequency to energy. ℏ = h/(2π): reduced Planck constant. kB: Boltzmann’s constant, converting temperature to an energy scale. G ≈ 6.674 × 10−11 m3kg−1s−2 h ≈ 6.626 × 10−34 J·s kB ≈ 1.381 × 10−23 J/K ≈ 8.617 × 10−5 eV/K mₑ ≈ 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kg is the electron mass; mₚ ≈ 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is the proton mass; mᵤ ≈ 1.661 × 10⁻²⁷ kg is the atomic mass constant. The elementary charge e ≈ 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C is distinct from the base e of exponential functions; context identifies which is meant. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. If a sphere doubles in radius, by what factors do its area and volume change? Show the answer and reasoning Area grows by 2² = 4; volume grows by 2³ = 8. The geometric constants cancel when taking ratios. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS These sources support the laws and numerical values; some use university-level mathematics.
